worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 431,500.00 = 431,500.00. Federal taxable income = 431,500.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 400,000.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing jointly. Line 9 federal AGI 431,500.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 31,500.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 431,500.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 55,000.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15 PIT-ADJ deductions and exemptions 0.00. Line 17 = 431,500.00 + 0.00 - 31,500.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 400,000.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 400,000.00 = 400,000.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 400,000.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 8,000.00 = 120 + 3.2% x 17,000.00 = 544 + 4.3% x 25,000.00 = 1,075 + 4.7% x 50,000.00 = 2,350 + 4.9% x 215,000.00 = 10,535 + 5.9% x 85,000.00 = 5,015; total 19,639, to the cent 19,639.00. The printed section on T-7 gives 19,637.00; expected keeps the schedule figure 19,639.00, 2.00 more. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 19,639.00.
accepted_approximations: Over 100,000 the printed section is base plus rate, and each base is the table's last row (midpoint 99,950), not the tax at 100,000. A bracket schedule cannot hold that step down, so the schedule gives more than the printed section at every income over 100,000.
